args.title: Fix export file name to use local date for the export day
args.body:
File: src/exportUtils.ts

Change formatExportFilename to accept and use the local date for the export day rather than UTC date from at.toISOString, so that the filename reflects the day of export in the user's own time zone, not always the next day in UTC.

label: bug
file: src/exportUtils.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The filename for exports uses toISOString() which encodes dates in UTC, causing evening exports in US time zones to roll to the next day. The fix is to format the date part of the filename from the local time to match the export day in the user's time zone.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

Transaction amounts are stored as BIGINTs representing minor units (e.g. cents). This approach avoids floating point rounding errors. The 'amount' column is bigint in the database and parsed as integers in code. Currencies without cents, like the yen, are handled by storing whole units as integers, so no decimal or float rounding occurs.

args.title: Fix truncated report name on duplicate - use (copy) suffix correctly
args.body:
File: src/api/reports.ts

The duplicate report API truncates the original report's name to 120 characters before adding the suffix `(copy)`, causing the suffix to be replaced by `...` when near the limit. Fix by appending `(copy)` after truncation to ensure the suffix is visible, avoiding confusing duplicate names.

Duplicating a report with a name close to the max length truncates the name before adding `(copy)`, causing the suffix to be replaced by ellipsis `...`. The fix is to append `(copy)` after truncation to clearly differentiate the duplicate from the original.
